(cancel-request! slot)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/requests.scm:33

Cancel the request in flight in SLOT, if any.
Its result is never delivered.

(candidate text #:suffix (suffix #f) #:annotation (annotation "") #:target (target #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/minibuffer.scm:57

Return a candidate of the minibuffer, showing TEXT.

(candidate-annotation record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/minibuffer.scm:52

candidate-target.description:
(candidate-target record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/minibuffer.scm:53

Return the `target` field of RECORD, a `candidate` record.

candidate-text.description:
(candidate-text record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/minibuffer.scm:49

(char-start text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:798

column.description:
(column text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:832

Return the column of POSITION in TEXT, in graphemes from 0.

command.description:
(command name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:115

Return the procedure of the command NAME; it is an error if none.

command-names.description:
(command-names)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:120

Return the names of the commands defined.

completing-read.description:
(completing-read s prompt source #:accept (accept take-target) #:preview (preview #f) #:initial (initial "") #:pattern (pattern (lambda (input) input)) #:require-match (require-match #t) #:abort (abort #f) #:keymap (keymap #f) #:select-input (select-input #f) #:history (history #f) #:remember (remember (quote choice)))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/minibuffer.scm:188

Read a choice in the minibuffer of session S with PROMPT and INITIAL.
SOURCE is a list of candidates (strings or `candidate`s), a
`candidate-table` (for many), a procedure from the input to a list,
or an `async-source`.
On \[minibuffer-accept],
(ACCEPT session candidate) is called with the selected candidate, or
one made of the input when nothing matches and REQUIRE-MATCH is false
(\[minibuffer-accept-input] takes the input as it is); by default,
the default action on the candidate's target is done. PREVIEW, if
given, is called the same way for each candidate selected while
reading; \[minibuffer-abort] undoes what it did to the panes, and
calls ABORT, if given, for what else they did. PATTERN gives the part
of the input candidates are matched against (the file name after its
directory). KEYMAP, if given, holds the keys of what is being read
(a file name's, say): it is looked up before `minibuffer-map`.
SELECT-INPUT, if given, is a procedure (input) saying when the input
itself is selected first rather than the first candidate, as vertico
selects an existing directory's name. HISTORY, if given, is the name
of the history \[minibuffer-previous-history] and
\[minibuffer-next-history] go through, a symbol; what is taken is
remembered there: the input completed with the candidate taken, or,
with REMEMBER `input`, the input as typed (a search's words, not the
line found). REMEMBER can also be a procedure (entry candidate)
returning what to remember of the candidate taken instead of ENTRY,
the input completed with it, or #f for nothing (a directory gone
into). The procedures run in the scope this is called in, as the
command calling it does.

copy-file.description:
(copy-file from to)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:653

Copy the file or directory FROM to TO, which must not exist.
A directory is copied with all it holds, a symbolic link as
a link.

current-buffer.description:
(current-buffer s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:84

Return the buffer of the focused pane of S, whatever has the keys.

current-prefix.description:
(current-prefix s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:222

Return the prefix argument the running command of S was given.
As Emacs has it: #f, (4) for `C-u` (16 for `C-u C-u`...), a number,
or - for a bare minus.

current-session.description:
(current-session)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:176

Return the session whose input is handled, or was last.
That is the one evaluated code acts on; #f with no frontend attached.

default-directory.description:
(default-directory s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:308

Return the directory of the focused pane's file in S, with a slash.
Without a file, it is the directory its buffer's mode says (a
directory's listing is in that directory), else the working directory.

define-action.description:
define-action: macro, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:60

Define the action NAME on targets of KIND.
It is a procedure of the session S and the target's value V; DOC
documents both the procedure and the action.

define-command.description:
define-command: macro, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:137

Define the command NAME, a procedure of the session S and the count N.
DOC documents both the procedure and the command; BODY runs when it is
invoked.

define-hook.description:
define-hook: macro, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:61

Declare the hook NAME, documented by DOC.
DOC says when it runs and what its procedures are called with.

define-key!.description:
(define-key! map keys binding)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/keymaps.scm:102

Bind KEYS, a key description, to BINDING in MAP.
A binding made in a scope other than the root is owned by it: shutting
the scope removes it, unless it has been rebound since. While a package
loads, the binding waits until the package is published. KEYS bound as
the prefix of longer bindings stays a prefix while they last.

define-minor-mode.description:
define-minor-mode: macro, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:205

Define the minor mode NAME, documented by DOC.
The other arguments are keywords, as `register-minor-mode!` takes them.

define-mode.description:
define-mode: macro, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:187

Define the major mode NAME, documented by DOC.
The other arguments are keywords, as `register-mode!` takes them.

define-option.description:
define-option: macro, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:267

Declare the option NAME, its DEFAULT and documentation DOC.
The other arguments are keywords, as `register-option!` takes them.

define-view.description:
define-view: macro, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:179

Define the command NAME showing a view of the rows BODY gives.
DOC documents it. RET does the default action on a row's target and
\[view-refresh] shows the rows again.

delete-path.description:
(delete-path path recursive)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:663

Delete the file or directory at PATH.
A directory must be empty unless RECURSIVE; a symbolic link
is deleted, not what it points to.

delete-path-and-buffers!.description:
(delete-path-and-buffers! s path)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:99

Delete the file or directory PATH, with all it holds, in session S.
The buffers of the open files deleted are killed. It is an error, and
nothing is deleted, when one of them has unsaved edits: they would be
left with no file to be recovered against.

derived-mode?.description:
(derived-mode? name ancestor)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:217

Return #t if the mode NAME is ANCESTOR or extends it.

directory-list.description:
(directory-list directory)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:630

Return the entries of DIRECTORY, sorted.
Subdirectories have a slash after their name.

display-buffer!.description:
(display-buffer! s d)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:421

Show the document D in a pane of S without leaving the focused one.
That is the pane showing it already, else a new one below.

doc.description:
(doc s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:22

Return the document the commands of session S act on.

document-buffer.description:
(document-buffer d)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:70

Return the buffer of the document D, or #f.
Its identity is the document's: the list holds the document, so the
address is not reused while it is there.

document-datum-before.description:
(document-datum-before text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:685

Return the span (start end) of the datum before POSITION in TEXT.
It is the last datum ending before POSITION in the innermost list
around it, as Emacs's `eval-last-sexp` takes it; #f if none.

document-dirty?.description:
(document-dirty? text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:492

Return #t if TEXT is a document with edits not yet saved.

document-forms.description:
(document-forms text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:675

Return the spans (start end) of the top-level data of TEXT.
They are read as the VM reads them, up to a malformed datum.

document-grant.description:
(document-grant document right #:to service #:actor (actor #f))  procedure, <techne-editor access>:2

Grant SERVICE DOCUMENT with RIGHT; return the grant, a number.
RIGHT is read, to have snapshots of its text, or stage, to propose
changes too, which wait for someone to accept them as edits by ACTOR
(service: and the service's name if not given). Pass the grant to
`service-call` where a document would go: the service's snapshot names
it (`snapshot-grant`). It holds while the service's world does, until
`grant-revoke!`.

document-id.description:
(document-id text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:476

Return a number identifying TEXT, a document or a presentation.
Each handle Lisp gets is a new object; compare texts by this.

document-length.description:
(document-length text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:484

Return the length of TEXT in bytes.

document-limit-history!.description:
(document-limit-history! document revisions)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:456

Keep at most REVISIONS of DOCUMENT's history, or all of it when
REVISIONS is #f: a log's, which would otherwise keep every line
it ever had, deleted ones too. Older revisions are forgotten,
with what undo could reverse there. Refused for a file's document,
whose journal keeps it whole.

document-lines.description:
(document-lines text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:563

Return every line of TEXT as (start line number).
LINE is without its line break; numbers count from 1.

document-map-position.description:
(document-map-position text position revision)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:514

Return where POSITION of TEXT as of REVISION is now.
Return #f when that revision is no longer in the history.

document-path.description:
(document-path text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:496

Return the file TEXT was opened from, or #f.

document-prepare-relocation.description:
(document-prepare-relocation document path)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:584

Prepare DOCUMENT to follow its file when it moves to PATH.
PATH is the true name it will have (`file-truename`'s, which
may not exist yet). The journal of its unsaved edits there is
locked until `document-relocate!` or `relocation-cancel!`;
it is an error if it cannot be, or holds unsaved edits.

document-reload!.description:
(document-reload! document)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:615

Read DOCUMENT's file again if it changed on disk.
It is an edit by "disk", refused while DOCUMENT has unsaved
edits. Return #t if the text changed.

document-relocate!.description:
(document-relocate! document relocation)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:594

Make DOCUMENT follow its file, moved as RELOCATION prepared.
Saving writes there from now on. Return #f, or what kept its
journal where it was, which it is written in still.

document-revision.description:
(document-revision text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:488

Return the revision of TEXT, which each change increases.

document-save!.description:
(document-save! document)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:609

Write DOCUMENT to its file, refusing an external change.

document-save-overwriting!.description:
(document-save-overwriting! document)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:611

Write DOCUMENT to its file even if it changed on disk.

document-string.description:
(document-string text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:480

Return the whole of TEXT, a document or a presentation.

document-substring.description:
(document-substring text from to)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:500

Return the part of TEXT between the byte positions FROM and TO.

drop-buffer!.description:
(drop-buffer! s b)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:378

Take the buffer B off the buffer list, in session S.
Panes showing it, in S and in every other attached session, show the
next buffer, also those \[minibuffer-abort] in an open minibuffer
would bring back. A file's document stays open, with its unsaved edits.

edit!.description:
(edit! s edits group)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:43

Make EDITS, each (from to text), in session S as one change.
GROUP is `new` or `extend`, as `view-edit!` takes it.

emacs-map.description:
emacs-map = #<keymap #<hash-table> #f #<registry bindings #<hash-table> #<procedure>> #f>

The keys of the Emacs profile, after the modes'.

error-text.description:
(error-text e)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:187

Return what the error E says, for the echo area.
The VM's prefix naming a view native (view-edit! ...) is left out, as
Emacs says "Text is read-only".

eval-region!.description:
(eval-region! s from to)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/live.scm:87

Evaluate the text from FROM to TO of S's focused document; show it.
It is evaluated in the document's module, as part of its file; the
first time, that module is loaded from the document's text.

excerpt.description:
(excerpt d from to #:face (face #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:40

Return a run showing FROM to TO of document D, edited through to it.
FACE is how it is drawn, or #f.

explain-key.description:
(explain-key s keys state)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:386

Return what binds KEYS in session S and input STATE, the winner first.
KEYS is a list of keys. Each is (source binding): BINDING a command's
name or a keymap, a prefix; SOURCE where it is bound, as
`keymap-sources` names it. The first is what KEYS do; the others are
shadowed by it.

explain-option.description:
(explain-option b name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:295

Return the settings of the option NAME that apply in buffer B.
B #f means no buffer. Each is (cell value by), the one that wins first:
CELL is `buffer`, a mode's name, `global` or `default`; BY is who made
it (a package, `root` for the editor's own code and what is evaluated
in it, a mode for its own options).

file-attributes.description:
(file-attributes path)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:647

Return what is at PATH, or #f if nothing is there.
It is (kind size modified mode target): KIND `file`,
`directory`, `symlink` or `other`, a symbolic link not
followed; MODIFIED in seconds since the epoch; MODE the
permission bits; TARGET a link's target, else #f.

file-document.description:
(file-document path #:document (d #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/files.scm:58

Return the document of the file at PATH.
It is opened with its journal the first time; D, a document already
open, is registered as the file's.

file-head.description:
(file-head path bytes)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:667

Return the first BYTES bytes of the file at PATH, as text.
What is not UTF-8 is replaced; a character cut at the end is
left out.

file-location.description:
(file-location path line)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:105

Return the location of line LINE, from 1, of the file at PATH.

file-name.description:
(file-name path)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/files.scm:17

Return the part of PATH after its directory.

file-name-map.description:
file-name-map = #<keymap #<hash-table> #f #<registry bindings #<hash-table> #<procedure>> #f>

The keys of a file name being read, over the minibuffer's own.

file-truename.description:
(file-truename path)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:657

Return PATH absolute, its symbolic links and . and .. resolved.
A file that does not exist yet is named in its directory's
true name.

find-mode.description:
(find-mode name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:130

Return the mode NAME, or #f if there is none.

goto-next!.description:
(goto-next! s needle)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:276

Move point in session S to the next NEEDLE after it.

grant-revoke!.description:
(grant-revoke! grant)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/access.rs:245

Revoke GRANT: its service has no more snapshots through it, nor
proposes through it, and what it proposed is accepted only to
adopt it.

indent-lines!.description:
(indent-lines! s starts group)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/indent.scm:37

Indent the lines of S's document at STARTS as its buffer's mode does.
STARTS are sorted, or a procedure of no arguments giving them, called
only if the mode indents; the edits are one change, GROUP as `edit!`
takes it. Return #f if the mode does not indent.

indent-spec-set!.description:
(indent-spec-set! specs name n)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:711

Make the form named NAME, a string, have N distinguished
arguments in SPECS: they indent by 4, its body by 2. With N #f,
it is a call again (but names starting with \"def\" have a body).

indentation.description:
(indentation d p)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/indent.scm:19

Return the position of the first character not a blank on P's line.
P is a position of document D; the line's end if it is all blanks.

insert-text!.description:
(insert-text! s text group)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:129

Insert TEXT at every range of session S, replacing what it selects.
GROUP is `new` or `extend`, as `view-edit!` takes it.

kbd.description:
(kbd keys)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/keymaps.scm:30

Return the keys of KEYS, a key description such as `"C-x C-s"`.

keymap-sequences.description:
(keymap-sequences km)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/keymaps.scm:155

Return every key sequence bound in the keymap KM.
Each is a string as `kbd` reads it.

keymap-sources.description:
(keymap-sources s state)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:369

Return the keymaps keys are looked up in, in session S and STATE.
STATE is `chord` or `normal`; see the comment above for the order.

kill-ring.description:
(kill-ring s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:173

Return the kill ring, which S shares: (text . linewise?), newest first.

kill-save!.description:
(kill-save! s text linewise backward)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:208

Save TEXT as a kill in session S, joining it to a kill just made.
With LINEWISE it is whole lines; with BACKWARD it joins at the front.

line-candidate.description:
(line-candidate d pos #:annotation (annotation ""))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:431

Return a candidate for the line at POS of D.
Its text is the line, its annotation ANNOTATION and the line's number,
its target the line's location.

line-down.description:
(line-down text position count goal)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:838

Return the position COUNT lines below POSITION in TEXT.
A negative COUNT goes up; the position is at the column GOAL, or the
line's end if it is shorter.

line-end.description:
(line-end text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:827

Return the end of the line of POSITION in TEXT, before its break.

line-number.description:
(line-number text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:834

Return the line of POSITION in TEXT, counting from 1.

line-span.description:
(line-span text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:830

Return the span (start end) of the line of POSITION in TEXT.
It includes the line break.

line-start.description:
(line-start text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:825

Return the start of the line of POSITION in TEXT.

line-starts.description:
(line-starts d from to)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/indent.scm:28

Return the starts of the lines of document D from FROM to TO, in order.
They are FROM's line and those starting before TO.

lines-containing.description:
(lines-containing text needle fold limit)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:902

Return the starts of the lines of TEXT containing NEEDLE, in
order, at most LIMIT of them. With FOLD, letters match whatever
their case.

lines-matcher.description:
(lines-matcher text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:525

Return a matcher of the non-empty lines of TEXT.
`matcher-line` gives each entry's start and line number.

lisp-form-around.description:
(lisp-form-around text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:722

Return the span (start end) of the top-level form around POSITION
in TEXT, or the last before it: from the line opening a list in
its first column to where it closes, the text's end if it does
not. #f if there is none.

lisp-indent.description:
(lisp-indent d starts)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/indent.scm:111

Return the edits (from to text) indenting the lines at STARTS as Lisp.
STARTS are sorted line starts of document D.

lisp-indent-edits.description:
(lisp-indent-edits text starts specs)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:728

Return the edits (from to text) indenting the lines starting at
STARTS, sorted, in TEXT as Lisp: each replaces a line's leading
blanks. Lines right already, and in strings, are left.

listing-get.description:
(listing-get b key)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:33

Return the entry KEY of the state of listing B, or #f.

listing-goto!.description:
(listing-goto! s b key #:offset (offset 0))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:112

Put the caret of S's focused pane at the row KEY of listing B.
It goes OFFSET bytes into the row; nothing moves when there is no
such row.

listing-key-at.description:
(listing-key-at b pos)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:108

Return the key of the row at POS of listing B, or #f.

listing-mark.description:
(listing-mark b key)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:92

Return the mark of the row KEY of listing B, a character, or #f.

listing-marked.description:
(listing-marked b c)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:121

Return the targets of the rows of listing B marked with C, in order.

listing-redisplay!.description:
(listing-redisplay! b)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:76

Make the rows of listing B again, from what its state holds now.
Marks of rows no longer there are forgotten. Once the package that made
it is gone, the rows stay as they are.

listing-row.description:
(listing-row b key target . columns)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:98

Return the row KEY, a string, of listing B, standing for TARGET.
Its first column is its mark, COLUMNS follow. Only such rows are
marked; others, as headings, are passed over.

listing-set!.description:
(listing-set! b key value)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:37

Make VALUE the entry KEY of the state of listing B.

listing-targets.description:
(listing-targets s #:mark (c #\*))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:130

Return the targets the focused listing's command in S acts on.
They are those of the rows marked with C, else the row's at point; it
is an error if there are none.

listing?.description:
(listing? b)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:29

Return #t if B is a buffer whose state is a listing's.

location.description:
(location d pos #:revision (revision (document-revision d)))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:100

Return the location of POS in document D, as of REVISION.
REVISION is the document's revision now unless given.

location-document.description:
(location-document l)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:109

Return the document of the location L, opening its file if needed.

location-position.description:
(location-position l)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:114

Return where the location L is now, mapped past the edits since.

location?.description:
(location? obj)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:92

Return #t if OBJ is a `location` record.

lookup-key.description:
(lookup-key map keys)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/keymaps.scm:175

Return the binding of KEYS, a list of keys, in MAP.
That is a command's name, a keymap (KEYS is a prefix), or #f.

make-directory.description:
(make-directory path)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:659

Make the directory PATH, and those above it that are missing.

make-document.description:
(make-document text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:448

Return a new document holding TEXT, with no file.

make-generated-buffer!.description:
(make-generated-buffer! name d mode #:state (state #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:116

Return a new buffer NAME of the document D in MODE, with STATE.
LENS is the lens whose document D is, if any. A buffer of that name is
replaced.

make-indent-specs.description:
(make-indent-specs)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:707

Return a table of how forms indent, holding Scheme's own.
See `indent-spec-set!`.

make-keymap.description:
(make-keymap)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/keymaps.scm:66

Return a new keymap, without bindings.

make-listing-buffer!.description:
(make-listing-buffer! name mode make-rows #:state (state (quote ())))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/listings.scm:59

Return the listing NAME in MODE, made if there is none, made anew.
Its rows are (MAKE-ROWS buffer), made with `listing-row`. STATE is an
alist of the entries the package keeps in it, set each time; the marks
of a listing already there, in MODE or one extending it, stay.

make-matcher.description:
(make-matcher texts)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:522

Return a matcher of the strings TEXTS, for the minibuffer.
Entries are numbered from 0, in the order of TEXTS.

make-presentation.description:
(make-presentation)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1002

Return a new presentation, without rows.

make-request-slot.description:
(make-request-slot)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/requests.scm:21

Return a new request slot, with no request in flight.

make-service.description:
(make-service name file (deadline #f) #:files (files #f) #:memory (memory #f))  procedure, <techne-editor service>:2

Return a service named NAME, its world made from the Lisp file FILE.
The world is of its own, on a thread of its own, started when first
asked. Making it needs this world's loading capability, and its world
reads no more than this one may. Loading FILE, and each request, is
killed past DEADLINE milliseconds, ten seconds if not given. With
FILES, its world has the files capability too, which this one must
have, reading and writing as this one may: it can list and search
files (`project-files`, `search-file`). Its world holds MEMORY
megabytes at most, 512 if not given: past that, what it runs is
refused, as in any world. The current scope owns it: shutting the scope
closes it, as `service-close!` does.

make-view.description:
(make-view text actor)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:911

Return a new view of TEXT, a document or a presentation.
Its edits are recorded as ACTOR's.

matcher-copy.description:
(matcher-copy matcher)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:538

Return a matcher of MATCHER's entries that filters on its own.

matcher-filter!.description:
(matcher-filter! matcher pattern)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:536

Match PATTERN against MATCHER's entries; return how many match.
Each word of PATTERN must occur, without case unless it has an
upper-case letter.

matcher-find.description:
(matcher-find matcher text)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:547

Return the first entry of MATCHER whose text is TEXT, or #f.

matcher-line.description:
(matcher-line matcher entry)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:555

Return the start and line number of ENTRY of MATCHER.
MATCHER is a lines matcher; the result is a list (start number
text), numbers counting from 1, TEXT the index of its text.

matcher-match.description:
(matcher-match matcher k)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:543

Return the entry that match K of MATCHER's last pattern is.
K counts the matches from 0, in the entries' order.

matcher-size.description:
(matcher-size matcher)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:540

Return the number of entries of MATCHER.

matcher-text.description:
(matcher-text matcher entry)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:549

Return the text of ENTRY of MATCHER.

message!.description:
(message! s text)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:147

Show TEXT in the echo area of session S; #f clears it.
The message is kept in *Messages*.

minibuffer-history.description:
(minibuffer-history name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/minibuffer.scm:519

Return the entries of the minibuffer history NAME, newest first.

minibuffer-map.description:
minibuffer-map = #<keymap #<hash-table> #f #<registry bindings #<hash-table> #<procedure>> #f>

The keys of the minibuffer, in either profile.

modal-map.description:
modal-map = #<keymap #<hash-table> #f #<registry bindings #<hash-table> #<procedure>> #f>

The keys of normal state beyond Vim's, after the modes' normal keys.
The leader key, SPC, is bound in main.scm.

mode-chain.description:
(mode-chain name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:210

Return the mode NAME and its parents, nearest first.
Modes no longer defined end the chain.

mode-doc.description:
(mode-doc record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:100

Return the `doc` field of RECORD, a `mode` record.

mode-for-file.description:
(mode-for-file path)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:221

Return the major mode for a file at PATH.
That is the one with the longest suffix of PATH, else
`fundamental-mode`.

mode-map.description:
(mode-map name #:state (state (quote chord)))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:137

Return the keymap of the mode NAME for STATE, to bind keys in.
STATE is `chord` (the default) or `normal`.

mode-name.description:
(mode-name record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:99

Return the `name` field of RECORD, a `mode` record.

mode-names.description:
(mode-names)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:133

Return the names of the modes defined.

mode-on?.description:
(mode-on? s name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:340

Return #t if the minor mode NAME is on in the focused buffer of S.

mode-parent.description:
(mode-parent record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:102

Return the `parent` field of RECORD, a `mode` record.

move!.description:
(move! s to)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:37

Move the head of every range of session S to (TO head).
With the session's `extend` set (an active mark, visual mode) the
anchors stay; otherwise ranges collapse to carets.

move-path!.description:
(move-path! from to)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:70

Move the file or directory FROM to TO, which must not exist.
The open files moved with it follow: their unsaved edits stay, saving
writes where they are now, and their buffers are named anew. Nothing
moves when the journal of one of them cannot move with it. Return what
kept a journal where it was, a list of texts.

name-prefix!.description:
(name-prefix! map keys name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/keymaps.scm:79

Call the prefix KEYS of MAP NAME, as which-key shows it.
KEYS is a key description; it is an error if it is no prefix.

next-grapheme.description:
(next-grapheme text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:808

Return the position after the grapheme at POSITION in TEXT.

next-word-start.description:
(next-word-start text position style)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:816

Return the start of the word after POSITION in TEXT.
STYLE, "emacs" or "vim", says what a word is.

node-apply.description:
(node-apply node f . args)  procedure, <techne-node>:16

Call the remote procedure F on NODE with ARGS.
Each of ARGS is data or a remote value from NODE.

node-close.description:
(node-close node)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:416

Close the connection to NODE.

node-connect.description:
(node-connect command)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:409

Start COMMAND, a list of strings, and return the node it serves.
COMMAND runs `techne-node`, here or over ssh.

node-describe.description:
(node-describe node what)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:531

Return NODE's description of WHAT, a name or a remote value.

node-eval.description:
(node-eval node source #:module (module #f))  procedure, <techne-node>:10

Evaluate the string SOURCE on NODE, in its module MODULE.
MODULE is a name or a file's path, "user" by default. Print what the
evaluation printed and return its value: data, or a remote value.

node-interrupt.description:
(node-interrupt node)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:424

Interrupt what NODE is evaluating.

node-process.description:
(node-process node id)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:534

Return the process ID that NODE runs, to read from and write to again.

node-processes.description:
(node-processes node)  procedure, <techne-node>:26

Return the processes NODE runs, each an alist.
Its keys are `proc`, `pid`, `command`, `pty`, `persistent`, `status`
(`running` or how it exited) and `dropped` (the output bytes nobody
read).

node-shutdown.description:
(node-shutdown node)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:428

Ask NODE to end, with its processes.

node-transport-pid.description:
(node-transport-pid node)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:420

Return the id of the process carrying NODE's connection, or #f.

normal-directory.description:
(normal-directory path)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/files.scm:32

Return the directory PATH, absolute, without its . and .. parts.
They are taken away as written, a symbolic link not followed. The
result ends with a slash.

open-document.description:
(open-document path journal)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:465

Open the file at PATH as a document, journaling its edits to JOURNAL.
Unsaved edits found in JOURNAL are replayed.

open-file.description:
(open-file path)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:618

Return the file at PATH as a document, with its unsaved edits.
The edits come from its journal in the state directory.

option.description:
(option b name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:318

Return the value of the option NAME in buffer B, #f meaning no buffer.

point.description:
(point s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:28

Return the head of the primary range of session S: point.

pop-to-buffer!.description:
(pop-to-buffer! s b)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:146

Show the buffer B in a pane of S and focus it, keeping the focused one.
That is the pane showing B already, else the next pane, else a new one
below, which \[quit-window] closes, as Emacs shows help.

present!.description:
(present! p rows)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:70

Show ROWS in the presentation P; return a table of the rows by key.
Only what differs from what P shows changes.

presentation-key-at.description:
(presentation-key-at presentation position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1018

Return the key of the row of PRESENTATION at POSITION, or #f.

presentation-refresh!.description:
(presentation-refresh! presentation)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1028

Show the documents of PRESENTATION's excerpts as they are now.
This includes where they changed under it.

presentation-row-span.description:
(presentation-row-span presentation key)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1023

Return the span (start end) of the row KEY of PRESENTATION, or #f.
It is without the line break.

presentation-set-rows!.description:
(presentation-set-rows! presentation rows)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1014

Make ROWS what PRESENTATION shows, changing its text where they differ.
A row is (key column ...), its key a string, unique; a column is a
run or a list of runs, a run a string, (text face), or an excerpt
(document from to [face]). Carets on a row that stays follow it.

presentation-source-at.description:
(presentation-source-at presentation position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1040

Return where POSITION of PRESENTATION is in an excerpt's document.
The result is (document position): in the excerpt at POSITION, else
the first of its row (for a position in its label); #f if none.

presentation-sources.description:
(presentation-sources presentation)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1032

Return the documents PRESENTATION's excerpts show, each once.

presentation?.description:
(presentation? obj)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:1007

Return #t if OBJ is a presentation.

prev-grapheme.description:
(prev-grapheme text position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:810

Return the position of the grapheme before POSITION in TEXT.

process-close-input.description:
(process-close-input process)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:811

Close the input of PROCESS, which then reads end of file.

process-dropped.description:
(process-dropped process)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:821

Return how many bytes of PROCESS's output were dropped, unread.

process-exited?.description:
(process-exited? process)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:823

Return #t if PROCESS has ended.

process-kill.description:
(process-kill process)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:771

Kill PROCESS and its process group.

process-pid.description:
(process-pid process)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:767

Return the operating system's id of PROCESS.

process-read.description:
(process-read process stream)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:803

Wait for the next output of PROCESS on STREAM, `stdout` or `stderr`.
Return it as a string, or the eof object once the stream is closed.

process-read-all.description:
(process-read-all p stream)  procedure, <techne-process>:18

Return everything STREAM, `stdout` or `stderr`, of P outputs, as text.
It reads to the end of the stream.

process-read-all-bytes.description:
(process-read-all-bytes p stream)  procedure, <techne-process>:25

Return everything STREAM, `stdout` or `stderr`, of P outputs, as bytes.
It reads to the end of the stream; the result is a bytevector.

process-read-bytes.description:
(process-read-bytes process stream)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:806

Wait for the next output of PROCESS on STREAM, as a bytevector.
STREAM is `stdout` or `stderr`; once it is closed, return the eof object.

process-resize.description:
(process-resize process rows columns)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:817

Tell PROCESS, on a terminal, that it has ROWS and COLUMNS.

process-signal.description:
(process-signal process signal)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:815

Send SIGNAL to PROCESS's group.
SIGNAL is one of the symbols `int`, `term`, `kill`, `hup`, `stop` and
`cont`.

process-spawn.description:
(process-spawn program args #:pty (pty #f) #:node (node #f) #:persist (persist #f))  procedure, <techne-process>:2

Start PROGRAM with the list of strings ARGS; return the process.
It runs with pipes or, with PTY, on a terminal; here, or on NODE. With
PERSIST, on a node session, it survives disconnects, keeping its newest
output. The current scope owns a local process: shutting the scope
kills it.

process-wait.description:
(process-wait process)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:819

Wait for PROCESS to end; return its exit code, or (signal N).

process-write.description:
(process-write process data)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-process/src/lib.rs:809

Write DATA, a string or bytevector, to the input of PROCESS.
It waits while the input is full.

project-root.description:
(project-root dir)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/projects.scm:18

Return the root of the project the directory DIR is in.
That is the nearest directory up from DIR with a .jj or .git in it,
else DIR itself; with a slash, as DIR has.

proposal-accept!.description:
(proposal-accept! proposal #:seen (seen #f) #:adopt (adopt #f))  procedure, <techne-editor access>:12

Make PROPOSAL's changes as one edit; return the new revision.
They are moved past what changed since, and made by the grant's actor:
refused, saying by whom, if that touched the same text, and refused if
the text changed since revision SEEN, given (what `proposal-preview`
showed). A revoked grant's proposal is accepted only to ADOPT it, on
this world's authority.

proposal-file!.description:
(proposal-file! service grant base edits note)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/access.rs:254

File what SERVICE proposes through GRANT, held by it: EDITS, each
(from to text), of the text at revision BASE, with a NOTE saying
what for. Return the proposal, a number.

proposal-note.description:
(proposal-note proposal)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/access.rs:286

Return PROPOSAL's note.

proposal-preview.description:
(proposal-preview proposal)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/access.rs:295

Return PROPOSAL's changes as they would be made now, as
(revision ((from to text) ...)): the revision they are of, and
each change of the text at it. Refused, saying by whom, if what
changed since touched the same text.

proposal-reject!.description:
(proposal-reject! proposal)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/access.rs:334

Reject PROPOSAL: it is not made, nor offered any more.

proposal-state.description:
(proposal-state proposal)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/access.rs:273

Return what PROPOSAL is: pending, revoked (its grant was, or its
service's world ended), applied or rejected; decided long ago,
it is no longer known.

proposals.description:
(proposals document)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/access.rs:262

Return the proposals for DOCUMENT waiting to be decided, oldest
first.

ranges.description:
(ranges s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:25

Return the ranges of the selection of session S, each (anchor head).

read-directory-name.description:
(read-directory-name s prompt initial accept)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:318

Read a directory's name in the minibuffer of S with PROMPT and INITIAL.
It is completed a directory at a time, as `read-file-name` completes:
the candidates are ./, the directory of the input itself, then ../ and
the subdirectories. Taking ./ calls (ACCEPT session directory) with its
absolute name, with a slash; taking another goes into it.
\[minibuffer-accept-input] takes the input as it is, also a directory
that does not exist yet.

read-file-name.description:
(read-file-name s prompt initial accept)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:281

Read a file name in the minibuffer of S with PROMPT and INITIAL.
The name is completed a directory at a time: the candidates are the
entries of the input's directory. Taking a directory goes into it;
(ACCEPT session path) gets a file's absolute path, also one that does
not exist yet. The input naming a directory that exists is selected
first, as vertico selects it: taking it as it is gives ACCEPT the
directory's path, with its slash.

region-text.description:
(region-text s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:256

Return the text of the region of session S, its primary range.

register-command!.description:
(register-command! name doc proc)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:109

Make PROC, a procedure of a session and a count, the command NAME.
DOC documents it. The current scope owns the command.

register-minor-mode!.description:
(register-minor-mode! name doc #:keys (keys (quote ())) #:normal (normal (quote ())) #:layer (layer #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:192

Define the minor mode NAME, documented by DOC.
It is on where the boolean option NAME is. KEYS and NORMAL are
(key-description command) bindings for chords and for modal normal
state, LAYER a procedure (document from to) giving highlights (from to
face). It defines the command NAME, which turns the mode on and off in
the focused buffer.

register-mode!.description:
(register-mode! name doc #:parent (parent (quote fundamental-mode)) #:files (files (quote ())) #:keys (keys (quote ())) #:normal (normal (quote ())) #:layer (layer #f) #:target-at (target-at #f) #:complete (complete #f) #:indent (indent #f) #:directory (directory #f) #:options (options (quote ())))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:162

Define the major mode NAME, documented by DOC, extending PARENT.
It has PARENT's keys, layers and options, and its own: KEYS and NORMAL
are (key-description command) bindings for chords and for modal normal
state, a string in place of the command naming a prefix, LAYER a
procedure (document from to) giving highlights (from to face),
TARGET-AT a procedure (buffer position) giving the target there,
COMPLETE a procedure (buffer position) giving what completes the text
before it, (start . candidates), INDENT a procedure (document starts)
giving the edits (from to text) that indent the lines at STARTS,
DIRECTORY a procedure (buffer) giving the directory the buffer is in,
with its slash, for a buffer of no file (a directory's listing); OPTIONS
an alist of (option . value) set in the mode, FILES the file name
suffixes it is for. It defines the command NAME, which gives the focused
buffer this mode.

register-option!.description:
(register-option! name default doc #:type (type (quote any)))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:258

Declare the option NAME, its DEFAULT and its documentation DOC.
TYPE is the schema of its values, as `valid?` takes it: boolean, natural,
(one-of value ...), (or schema ...) and so on.

relocation-cancel!.description:
(relocation-cancel! relocation)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:590

Give up RELOCATION, unlocking the journal it prepared.

remote-value-written.description:
(remote-value-written remote)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:438

Return the node's bounded written preview of REMOTE.
At a data limit this is a fixed marker, not a readable datum.

remote-value?.description:
(remote-value? obj)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-node/src/lib.rs:433

Return #t if OBJ is a value held by a node.

remove-hook!.description:
(remove-hook! hook name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:81

Remove the procedure added to HOOK as NAME.

rename-file.description:
(rename-file from to)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:649

Move the file or directory FROM to TO, which must not exist.

replace-region!.description:
(replace-region! s f)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:261

Replace the text of every range of session S by (F text).
It is one undo unit.

request!.description:
(request! slot produce deliver #:fail (fail #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/requests.scm:41

Run (PRODUCE) in a task, cancelling the request SLOT had in flight.
When it returns, call (DELIVER result), unless a newer request was made
in SLOT since. When PRODUCE raises, call (FAIL condition) instead, if
given. The task belongs to the current scope.

request-pending?.description:
(request-pending? slot)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/requests.scm:29

Return #t if SLOT has a request in flight.

row.description:
(row #:key (key #f) #:target (target #f) . columns)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:33

Return a row of a view of COLUMNS standing for TARGET.
A column is a string, or a list of runs, each a string, (text face) or
an `excerpt`. KEY identifies the row across refreshes; without it, its
first column's text does.

row-at.description:
(row-at p table pos)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:79

Return the row at POS of presentation P, or #f.
TABLE is the table of rows `present!` gave.

row-target.description:
(row-target record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:31

Return the `target` field of RECORD, a `row` record.

run-command.description:
(run-command s name n)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:225

Run the command NAME in session S with the count N.
What commands record for the next one (a kill to append to, a goal
column) moves from now to last here; an error becomes the message.
Return #t when the command finished, #f when it raised an error.

run-hook!.description:
(run-hook! s hook . args)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/dispatch.scm:85

Call each procedure added to HOOK, in the order added.
Each is called with the session S and ARGS; one that fails shows its
error in S, and the others still run.

search!.description:
(search! s needle from forward)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:246

Return the span (start end) of the next NEEDLE from FROM in S.
It searches forward, or with FORWARD #f backward, and raises an error
if there is none. Case is ignored as `fold-case-for` says.

search-all.description:
(search-all doc needle from to)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:271

Return the spans (start end) of NEEDLE in DOC starting from FROM to TO.
Case is ignored as `fold-case-for` says.

search-text.description:
(search-text text position needle forward fold)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:842

Return the span (start end) of the next NEEDLE from POSITION, or #f.
It searches TEXT forward or, with FORWARD #f, backward; with FOLD,
letters match whatever their case.

search-text-all.description:
(search-text-all text needle from to fold)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:889

Return the spans (start end) of NEEDLE in TEXT from FROM to TO.
With FOLD, letters match whatever their case.

search-text-regexp.description:
(search-text-regexp text position regexp forward)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:871

Return the span (start end) of the next REGEXP from POSITION, or #f.
It searches TEXT forward or, with FORWARD #f, backward: then the
match is the last before POSITION of those found, not overlapping,
from the start of TEXT. REGEXP is compiled by `regexp` of `(srfi 115)`.

search-text-regexp-all.description:
(search-text-regexp-all text regexp from to)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:875

Return the spans (start end) of REGEXP's matches in TEXT.
The matches start from FROM to before TO and do not overlap; empty
ones are left out.

service-close!.description:
(service-close! service)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:559

Close SERVICE: its world is stopped, and requests fail from now
on. What shutting the scope that made it does.

service-closed?.description:
(service-closed? service)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:561

Return #t if SERVICE was closed.

service-info.description:
(service-info service)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:573

Return what SERVICE is, a dict: its name; its state (starting,
idle, running a request, failed to load its file, ended by
itself, stopped or closed); how many
times its world started and ended; how long the request running
has run (running-ms); the bytes its world held after its last
request (held), and may hold (memory); its deadline; the grants
it holds; and how its last request failed and why its last
world ended, if they did.

service-name.description:
(service-name service)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:549

Return SERVICE's name.

service-restart!.description:
(service-restart! service)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:556

Stop SERVICE's world, and start another now.

service-starts.description:
(service-starts service)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:547

Return how many times SERVICE's world was started.

service-stop!.description:
(service-stop! service)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:554

Stop SERVICE's world: what it runs is killed, and its queued
requests fail. It starts again, a new world, at the next
request; documents granted to the stopped one are not the new
one's.

services.description:
(services)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/service.rs:577

Return the services made, but closed ones, oldest first.

session-buffer.description:
(session-buffer s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:88

Return the buffer the commands of S act on.
That is the focused pane's, or #f while they edit the minibuffer's
input.

session-document.description:
(session-document s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:155

Return the document of the view the commands of session S act on.

session-focus.description:
(session-focus s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:47

Return the index of the focused pane of session S.

session-panes.description:
(session-panes s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:44

Return the views the panes of session S show, in order.

session-tree.description:
(session-tree s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:61

Return how the panes of session S tile the frame.
A leaf is a pane's index; a split is (split dir parts), DIR `below` or
`right` and PARTS a list of (share . tree), the shares summing to 1.

session-view.description:
(session-view s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:150

Return the view the commands of session S act on.
That is the focused pane's, or the minibuffer's input while it is
open.

set-buffer-mode!.description:
(set-buffer-mode! record value)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:52

Set the `mode` field of RECORD, a `buffer` record, to VALUE.

set-buffer-name!.description:
(set-buffer-name! record value)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:49

Set the `name` field of RECORD, a `buffer` record, to VALUE.

set-buffer-state!.description:
(set-buffer-state! record value)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:53

Set the `state` field of RECORD, a `buffer` record, to VALUE.

set-indent!.description:
(set-indent! name n)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/indent.scm:105

Make the form NAME indent its first N arguments by 4, its body by 2.
NAME is a symbol, as Emacs's `scheme-indent-function` property is put;
with N #f it indents as a call. Names starting with "def" have a body.

set-option!.description:
(set-option! name value #:buffer (b #f) #:mode (mode #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:279

Set the option NAME to VALUE in buffer B or the major mode MODE.
Without either, it is set globally.

set-session-panes!.description:
(set-session-panes! s views focus)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:51

Make VIEWS the panes of session S, the one at FOCUS focused.
With as many views as the tiling has panes, the tiling stays; else
the panes are stacked evenly. A view another attached session shows
is split, so that S gets a view of its own.

set-session-tree!.description:
(set-session-tree! s tree)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:66

Make TREE the tiling of the panes of session S.

set-view-read-only!.description:
(set-view-read-only! view read-only)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:987

Make VIEW refuse edits if READ-ONLY is true.

sget.description:
(sget s k)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:19

Return the value of the key K in the session S, or #f.

show-buffer!.description:
(show-buffer! s b #:remember (remember #t))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:135

Show the buffer B in the focused pane of S.
It is shown in the view it was last shown in, unless another pane, of
S or of another attached session, shows that one. With REMEMBER #f (a
preview) the buffer list's order stays.

show-document!.description:
(show-document! s d #:remember (remember #t))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:130

Show the document D in the focused pane of S, as `show-buffer!` does.
REMEMBER is as `show-buffer!` takes it.

show-in-other-pane!.description:
(show-in-other-pane! s d)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:407

Show the document D in a new pane of S below the focused one.
The new pane is focused.

show-lens!.description:
(show-lens! s name rows #:mode (mode (quote lens-mode)) #:state (state #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/lens.scm:33

Show a lens of ROWS in S's focused pane as the buffer NAME.
Return its view. ROWS are a view's, with excerpts. The buffer is in
MODE, with STATE, and replaces a buffer of that name.

show-view!.description:
(show-view! s name make-rows #:mode (mode (quote rows-mode)) #:data (data #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/views.scm:123

Show in S the view NAME, whose rows (MAKE-ROWS session) gives.
Its mode is MODE, `rows-mode` or one extending it, keeping DATA.

sset!.description:
(sset! s k v)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/session.scm:22

Store V as the value of the key K in the session S.

string->regexp.description:
(string->regexp pattern)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:882

Return the regular expression PATTERN, written as Perl and Rust's
regex crate write them, compiled, for `string-search-regexp`
and `search-text-regexp`, and as the regexps of `(srfi 115)`;
it has no SRE, so `regexp->sre` of it is #f.

string-search-regexp.description:
(string-search-regexp string regexp)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:866

Return the span (start end) of REGEXP's first match in STRING, or #f.
The span is in bytes.

take-target.description:
(take-target s c)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/minibuffer.scm:596

Do the default action on the target of candidate C in session S.
This is how `completing-read` accepts by default.

target.description:
(target kind value)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:26

Make a `target` record.
Its fields are KIND and VALUE.

target-at.description:
(target-at d pos)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:126

Return the target at POS in document D, or #f.
It is found by D's buffer's mode, if that finds any.

target-kind.description:
(target-kind record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:28

Return the `kind` field of RECORD, a `target` record.

target-value.description:
(target-value record)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:29

Return the `value` field of RECORD, a `target` record.

target?.description:
(target? obj)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/targets.scm:26

Return #t if OBJ is a `target` record.

tcp-accept.description:
(tcp-accept listener)  procedure, <techne-net>:11

Wait for a connection to LISTENER and return it.
The current scope owns the connection: shutting the scope closes it.

tcp-close.description:
(tcp-close socket)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:585

Close SOCKET, a connection or a listener, if it is open.
Tasks waiting on it fail.

tcp-close-output.description:
(tcp-close-output connection)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:577

Close the sending side of CONNECTION: the peer reads end of file.
Reading from CONNECTION goes on.

tcp-closed?.description:
(tcp-closed? socket)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:596

Return #t if SOCKET, a connection or a listener, is closed.

tcp-connect.description:
(tcp-connect host port)  procedure, <techne-net>:16

Connect to PORT on HOST, a name or an IP address; return the connection.
The current scope owns the connection: shutting the scope closes it.

tcp-connection?.description:
(tcp-connection? obj)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:624

Return #t if OBJ is a TCP connection.

tcp-listen.description:
(tcp-listen port #:host (host "127.0.0.1") #:backlog (backlog 1024) #:reuse-port (reuse-port #f))  procedure, <techne-net>:2

Return a listener for TCP connections to PORT on HOST.
HOST is an IP address ("0.0.0.0" or "::" for every interface) or
"localhost"; PORT 0 picks a free port, which `tcp-local-address` tells.
BACKLOG connections wait to be accepted at most. With REUSE-PORT, other
listeners may share the port, and the kernel spreads connections over them.
The current scope owns the listener: shutting the scope closes it.

tcp-listener?.description:
(tcp-listener? obj)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:628

Return #t if OBJ is a TCP listener.

tcp-local-address.description:
(tcp-local-address socket)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:607

Return the address of SOCKET, a connection or a listener, here.
It is a list of the host, a string, and the port.

tcp-peer-address.description:
(tcp-peer-address connection)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:618

Return the address of the peer of CONNECTION.
It is a list of the host, a string, and the port.

tcp-read.description:
(tcp-read connection)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:569

Wait for data from CONNECTION and return it as a string.
Return the eof object once the peer has closed its side. Bytes that
are not UTF-8 read as U+FFFD; a character split between two reads is
returned whole, with the second.

tcp-read-bytes.description:
(tcp-read-bytes connection)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-net/src/lib.rs:572

Wait for data from CONNECTION and return it as a bytevector.
Return the eof object once the peer has closed its side.

tcp-write.description:
(tcp-write connection data)  procedure, <techne-net>:21

Write DATA, a string or a bytevector, to CONNECTION.
It waits until the kernel has taken all of it, so a peer that reads
slowly makes it wait. DATA is sent from where it is, not copied:
changing it meanwhile changes what is sent.

texts-lines-matcher.description:
(texts-lines-matcher texts)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:529

Return a matcher of the non-empty lines of each of TEXTS, in
order. `matcher-line` gives each entry's start and line number in
its text, and the index of its text in TEXTS.

toggle-mode!.description:
(toggle-mode! s name)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:345

Turn the minor mode NAME on or off in the focused buffer of S.

unset-option!.description:
(unset-option! name #:buffer (b #f) #:mode (mode #f))  procedure, @lisp@/editor/modes.scm:288

Take back the setting of the option NAME in buffer B or mode MODE.
Without either, the global setting is taken back.

view-document.description:
(view-document view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:934

Return the text VIEW shows: a document or a presentation.

view-edit!.description:
(view-edit! view edits group)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:967

Make EDITS, each (from to text), in VIEW's document as one change.
GROUP is "new" for a new undo unit or "extend" to join the last one.
Return the new revision; raise an error if the edit is refused (the
view is read-only, or a lens cannot make it).

view-edit-at!.description:
(view-edit-at! view base edits group)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:977

Make EDITS, made against the text at revision BASE, in VIEW.
They are moved past what changed since, or refused, saying by whom,
when that touched the same text. This is for a command that looked at
the text, waited, then edits what it saw. GROUP is as `view-edit!`
takes it. Return the new revision.

view-id.description:
(view-id view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:919

Return a number identifying VIEW; compare views by it.

view-primary.description:
(view-primary view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:944

Return the index of the primary range of VIEW's selection.

view-ranges.description:
(view-ranges view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:938

Return the ranges of VIEW's selection, each (anchor head).

view-read-only?.description:
(view-read-only? view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:983

Return #t if VIEW refuses edits.

view-redo!.description:
(view-redo! view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:995

Redo the last change undone in VIEW's document; return the revision.

view-scroll.description:
(view-scroll view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:923

Return the position of the first text VIEW shows.

view-set-ranges!.description:
(view-set-ranges! view ranges primary)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:949

Make RANGES, each (anchor head), the selection of VIEW.
PRIMARY is the index of the primary range.

view-set-scroll!.description:
(view-set-scroll! view position)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:927

Make VIEW show its document from POSITION.

view-split.description:
(view-split view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:915

Return a new view of VIEW's document with VIEW's carets and scroll.

view-undo!.description:
(view-undo! view)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:991

Undo the last change of VIEW's document; return the new revision.

visit!.description:
(visit! s path line column)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/buffers.scm:155

Show line LINE, column COLUMN, of the file PATH in S's focused pane.
Lines and columns count from 1. Where the pane was is remembered for
\[pop-definition].

word-end.description:
(word-end text position style)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:813

Return the end of the word at or after POSITION in TEXT.
STYLE, "emacs" or "vim", says what a word is.

word-object.description:
(word-object text position style around)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:823

Return the span (start end) of the word at POSITION in TEXT.
STYLE, "emacs" or "vim", says what a word is; with AROUND, the
space after it is included, as Vim's aw.

word-start.description:
(word-start text position style)  built-in procedure, @source@/crates/techne-editor/src/lib.rs:819

Return the start of the word at or before POSITION in TEXT.
STYLE, "emacs" or "vim", says what a word is.

yank-text.description:
(yank-text s)  procedure, @lisp@/editor/commands.scm:228

Return the newest kill of session S; it is an error if there is none.
